prompt:
PLAN 00 | PULLED OUT OF THE DARK
DURATION 15 SECONDS | HORIZONTAL 16:9

CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_RANDOM_PRISONER_A}} 
{{CHAR_RANDOM_PRISONER_B}}
{{CHAR_PALACE_GUARDS}}
{{CHAR_CELL_PRISONERS}}

LOCATION REFERENCES
{{LOC_CROWDED_HOLDING_CELL}}
{{LOC_CELL_SERVICE_CORRIDOR}}
{{LOC_PUBLIC_TRANSFER_ROUTE}} 

PROP REFERENCES
{{PROP_CELL_DOOR}}

Create a 15-second live-action cinematic sequence composed of four precisely timed handheld shots.

CHARACTER IDENTITIES

Prisoner A and Prisoner B are two unrelated young adult male captives with distinct identities, rigid handmade masks and worn captive clothing.

Preserve each referenced identity, costume, proportions and mask throughout the sequence.

The masks remain securely attached to their heads. Mask surfaces, edges and eye openings retain their exact shape. Emotion is expressed through visible eyes, breathing, hands, posture and interrupted movement.

Two guards conduct the transfer:
Guard One controls Prisoner A.
Guard Two controls Prisoner B.

At least twelve additional adult male prisoners remain crowded inside the cell. Their individual masks and clothing belong to the same visual world while retaining distinct designs.

The selection has already happened before the opening frame. Begin during the physical extraction of the two prisoners.

LOCATION AND LIGHT

A low, overcrowded holding cell beneath the palace. Old Iranian masonry, shallow rounded openings, worn stone surfaces and a heavy functional door.

Prisoners fill nearly all the available floor space. Some stand pressed against the walls; others sit beneath them with knees drawn inward. Layers of shoulders, masks and hands make the crowd’s density visible.

One weak recessed service lamp outside the cell sends a narrow strip of cold neutral light through the open doorway. It illuminates fragments of bodies while the deeper cell remains dark.

The doorway leads into a narrow service corridor running straight toward a broader public transfer route.

Widely spaced recessed practical lamps create alternating patches of illumination and darkness along the corridor.

Broader neutral architectural light spills from the public route at the far end. Both spaces are indoors.

Reference images anchor architecture, materials and design. The written lighting instructions determine the actual illumination and exposure.

Preserve restrained exposure and readable texture within deep shadow.

START STATE AND BLOCKING

The cell door is already open, resting against the corridor wall.

Prisoner A and Prisoner B stand near the doorway, still surrounded by other captives.

Guard One already grips Prisoner A’s upper arm.
Guard Two already grips Prisoner B’s upper arm.

The guards pull them toward the exit. The surrounding prisoners turn sideways and withdraw their hands to make a narrow passage.

The camera begins inside the cell, partly trapped behind a nearby prisoner’s shoulder.

Travel progresses continuously from the cell, through the corridor, toward the public route.

In frontal views looking back toward the cell:
Prisoner A is screen left.
Prisoner B is screen right.
Their guards remain on the outer sides of the pair.

In rear views looking toward the public opening:
Prisoner A is screen right.
Prisoner B is screen left.
Their guards remain on the outer sides.

At the narrow doorway, Prisoner A and Guard One pass first. Prisoner B and Guard Two follow half a step behind.

SHOT 00-01 | 0s–4s | 4 SECONDS

28mm handheld at shoulder height inside the cell, diagonally behind the prisoners and facing the open doorway.

A nearby captive’s shoulder initially obscures part of the frame. Beyond it, the guards are already pulling the two selected men through the crowded bodies.

The camera shifts sideways into a small gap.

Prisoner A reaches the doorway and presses his free palm against the stone jamb, instinctively resisting the forward pull. His fingers drag across the surface as Guard One forces him onward.

Behind him, Prisoner B draws his elbows inward as he is squeezed between another captive and Guard Two. He turns his masked head back toward the people remaining inside.

A seated prisoner pulls his feet clear of their path. Another captive presses his back against the wall.

The operator receives a small shoulder bump and makes a rough corrective tilt to find the departing men again.

Maintain readable glimpses of gripping hands, resisting posture and the crowded doorway through the foreground bodies.

Hard cut as Guard Two’s shoulder passes close to the lens.

SHOT 00-02 | 4s–7s | 3 SECONDS

35mm frontal handheld from the corridor just outside the doorway, looking back into the cell.

Prisoner A emerges screen left with Guard One on his outer side. Prisoner B follows screen right with Guard Two.

Prisoner A’s free hand slides off the jamb. His foot catches the threshold and his upper body pitches forward. Guard One’s existing grip pulls him upright while continuing to move.

Prisoner B crosses half a step later. His head remains turned toward the cell until Guard Two’s pull forces him to face forward and recover his balance.

The camera retreats two hurried short steps to avoid their approaching bodies. Framing briefly dips toward their arms before recovering to chest and mask height.

Through the doorway behind them, compressed layers of captives remain visible in the darkness.

Hard cut on Prisoner B’s first clear step into the corridor.

SHOT 00-03 | 7s–11s | 4 SECONDS

28mm close handheld from ahead of Prisoner B’s side of the group, moving backward through the corridor.

Prisoner B occupies the right foreground. Prisoner A is visible screen left, half a step ahead. Guard Two’s hand remains firmly wrapped around Prisoner B’s upper arm.

Prisoner B looks toward the gripping guard, then drops his gaze to find secure footing. His breathing is fast and broken. His free hand briefly clenches against his own clothing.

The camera makes a short lateral reframe toward Prisoner A.

Prisoner A keeps his neck rigid and eyes directed toward the route ahead. His shoulders tense with each forceful adjustment of Guard One’s grip.

The guards maintain a hurried, uneven walking pace. The prisoners struggle to keep their feet beneath them.

Camera movement follows the operator’s hurried footfalls: vertical jolts, small lateral corrections and a brief focus lag when a shoulder crosses close to the lens. Focus recovers on the prisoners’ masks and hands.

A recessed overhead lamp briefly reveals fabric texture and trembling fingers before the group enters another darker interval.

Hard cut while the group remains in motion.

SHOT 00-04 | 11s–15s | 4 SECONDS

32mm rear handheld from two meters behind the group, looking along the corridor toward the public opening.

Prisoner A is screen right.
Prisoner B is screen left.
Their guards occupy the outer sides.

Follow at upper-back height, framing the prisoners from approximately the knees upward. The corridor walls remain close on both sides.

Prisoner B gives one brief backward glance over his left shoulder toward the cell, revealing only a sliver of his mask profile. His hips and feet continue forward. Guard Two’s firm grip turns his attention back toward the route.

Prisoner A remains facing ahead. He takes a hurried extra step to recover from the guard’s pace.

The camera follows with an uneven walking rhythm, briefly drifting toward the wall before correcting behind the prisoners.

Ahead, the confined passage opens into a broader circulation space. More architectural light reaches their shoulders, and the acoustic space widens.

End as the prisoners’ leading feet cross the threshold into the public transfer route. Their bodies are still moving forward at the cut.

END STATE AND EDIT

The same two anonymous prisoners and the same two guards reach the public transfer route.

Guard One retains control of Prisoner A.
Guard Two retains control of Prisoner B.

Both prisoners remain frightened, walking under force. The other captives remain inside the cell.

The next block continues this transfer through the public space, retaining these two prisoners’ identities and clothing.

End on an active forward step for a direct movement cut into the next scene.

CAMERA AND PERFORMANCE

Each cut changes the camera’s physical position:
inside the crowded cell;
outside the doorway;
close ahead of the moving prisoners;
behind the group approaching the public route.

Handheld movement comes from the operator navigating bodies, retreating from approaching captives and keeping pace through the corridor.

Allow brief foreground obstruction and imperfect reframing while preserving the direction and meaning of the action.

The guards apply impatient, practiced force.

Prisoner A expresses fear through bodily resistance, a rigid neck and shallow breathing.

Prisoner B expresses fear through backward glances, uneven steps and a protective inward posture.

Their reactions occur at different moments. Background prisoners respond individually through withdrawn hands, lowered eyes and small shifts to make room.

Play the entire sequence at real-time speed.

SOUND

Inside the cell:
dense breathing;
restrained sobbing;
clothing rubbing against nearby bodies;
feet scraping stone.

At the threshold:
a shoe catching the edge;
a palm dragging across masonry;
fabric tightening beneath the guards’ hands.

In the corridor:
uneven footsteps;
strained breathing;
short reflections from close stone walls.

At the final opening:
distant footsteps and activity from the public route;
a gradually broader interior resonance.

NO MUSIC.
NO DIALOGUE.
